messages:
anna: canary multi-node TP rollout hung — 2/4 ranks stuck in allreduce after the kernel-selector change deployed last night. job=infra-tp-canary-17, started ~03:12 UTC. seeing AllReduce timeouts and KV cache size mismatch warnings.

diego: can you drop job id, cluster, model and tp/pp counts? :eyes:

anna: job=infra-tp-canary-17, cluster=eu-west-1a, model=redwood-7b-quant, tp=4, pp=1, batch_size=1

jess: @kevin any infra events for that cluster? i don't see node reboots but network jitter spiked.

kevin: no reboots. fabric monitoring shows a spike around 03:11-03:13 UTC. i'll pull switch logs and NIC errors.

mira: ran a quick perf trace on rank2 while it was stuck — snippet below. looks like AllReduce enters wait and never proceeds.

```
perf trace (rank2):
AllReduce start: 0.014s
waiting on peer 3 -> blocked at 0.42s
KV cache sync sizes observed: [1024, 1016, 1024, 1016]
Mismatch detected -> abort path triggered but not surfaced before timeout
```

perf-bot: profiling alert: tail-latency increased 3.4x after kernel-selector v2.1 (candidate PR #4721).

diego: KV cache lengths diverged — this smells like the batching heuristic change that disables prefix caching for short contexts. uneven cached sequence lengths -> different tensor shapes for allreduce.

anna: we tried reverting kernel-selector in canary but the hang persisted. suspect comm/compute overlap regression where the new kernel pad-to-vec results in different padded sizes across ranks.

jess: can we repro in a small cluster? ability to dump KV sizes just before allreduce would help. pinging @kevin for node access.

kevin: i pulled /var/log/tensor_comm.log from node-gpu-03. repeated messages:

```
[2026-03-18T03:12:45Z] rank0: EAGER_ALLREDUCE_TIMEOUT tensor_id=0x7f3a size=4096 peers=3
[2026-03-18T03:12:46Z] rank2: KV_CACHE_SYNC expected=1024 actual=1016
[2026-03-18T03:12:47Z] rank3: net_err=EPIPE retry=1
```

mira: i dug into kv_cache invalidation — the new kernel pad-to-vec optimization pads activations to multiples of 32 on some ranks (depending on micro-batching), while others get padded to 64. when we align tensors for the allreduce we rely on a global pad invariant that the change violates. i can sketch a small patch to coerce KV padding to a common granularity during TP sync.

anna: can we hotfix on canary? proposal: force KV padding to 64-multiple during TP sync and add an assert that logs expected vs actual sizes pre-allreduce. if folks agree i'll roll.

diego: +1 for hotfix and extra logging. also add a debug-only metadata tag so we can correlate future hangs to kernel-selector version.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-18-TP-HANG (#4567) — Sev2, assigned to eng-runtime.

jess: hotfix rolled to infra-tp-canary-17 at 03:28 UTC. two of three stuck jobs recovered immediately, one rank is still wedged. collecting a targeted perf trace for remaining rank.

mira: i'm opening PR to: 1) add pad-to-granularity step before KV sync, 2) add assert/log to allreduce entry, 3) unit test for kv-length invariants across TP.

anna: follow-ups: create end-to-end test that runs a tiny tp=4 job with kernel-selector combos, add changelog entry for v2.1, and bake the assert into non-prod builds. i'll update the canary run once PR is merged.

kevin: infra note — fabric vendor says there were low-level retransmits but not enough to explain the mismatch. looks like root cause is the padding divergence + batching heuristic.

jess: thumbs up. once patch lands let's run a 24h soak on canary to watch tail latencies and KV invariants. :thumbsup:

anna: thanks everyone — keeping INC open until we verify two successful soak windows.
